steps.question: How dense is the layout?
steps.why: Room around the text helps reading.
Rounded corners match the warm reading tone. Sharp corners feel technical next to long text.

steps.pick: radius.8: We use an 8px corner for buttons and inputs in order to mark their role as controls in a warm tone, by brand convention. A rounded radius does this by curving the edge enough to feel soft, while the sides stay straight. So controls feel friendly next to long text and never compete with it, because the brand is warm (brand.q1), corners are rounded (shape.values) and each screen holds one idea (content.q2).

steps.question: Which text roles does it need?
steps.why: A lead and a display role open articles.

steps.pick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 17.12:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: neutral.900: the strongest text step, 16.84:1 on surface.default, above the 4.5:1 floor.

steps.question: How many signals carry each meaning?
steps.why: Status is rare; color and a word are enough.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed gets its own value for touch.
A tint shows the choice clearly on warm paper.

steps.rule: The fill of a selected or current item, or a toggle that is on.
steps.pick: navy.light.100: a tint of the brand, 1.22:1 from content, always beside its edge (border.selected), so selection is never color alone.
steps.darkPick: navy.dark.100: a tint of the brand, 1.2:1 from content, always beside its edge (border.selected), so selection is never color alone.

steps.rule: The edge that marks a selected item, beside its fill, so selection is never color alone.
steps.pick: navy.light.600: the edge beside a selected fill, so selection is never color alone, 11.5:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: navy.dark.600: the edge beside a selected fill, so selection is never color alone, 6.86:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.

steps.question: Which states get their own visible value?
steps.why: Pressed gets its own value for touch.
Moderate speed feels calm in a slow reading flow. A fast flash feels jumpy.

steps.rule: The fill of the item the pointer or the keyboard is on, or whose submenu is open. A state shows on the item's background, one step from the surfaces it sits on: darker in light, and darker in dark too, as raised layers take the lighter step.
steps.pick: neutral.100, two steps darker than the surfaces it sits on (neutral.0), so the item under the pointer or the keyboard reads as a band without lifting off the page. It skips neutral.50, the page canvas, so a menu item never matches the page behind it.
steps.darkPick: neutral.0: We use a step darker than content for the item under the pointer or the keyboard in dark, in order to mark it as a band on both surfaces it meets: 1.1:1 on surface.default and 1.32:1 on surface.raised. The fill does this by stepping darker, as raised layers took the lighter step; muted text still reads 6.77:1 on it. So the hovered row or menu item shows on cards and menus alike, because hover and focus have their own look (accessibility.roles) and the neutral ramp sets the steps (color.definition).

steps.question: What contrast floor do we hold?
steps.why: AA contrast, with large text helping further.
Keyboard users must always see where they are.

steps.pick: navy.light.600: the focus ring, so the keyboard's place is never lost, 11.5:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.
steps.darkPick: navy.dark.600: the focus ring, so the keyboard's place is never lost, 6.86:1 on surface.default, above the 3:1 floor.

steps.pick: neutral.50, under content: 1.02:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.
steps.darkPick: neutral.0, under content: 1.1:1 from surface.default, so cards and panels stand forward.
